general_information.Description: The digital landscape is evolving at an unprecedented rate with unknown threats lurking around every corner. Cybersecurity resilience in the modern world cannot be just an addon - it's a necessity. Organizations must build cybersecurity resilience, and offensive security professionals like Ethical Hackers and Penetration Testers can help proactively discover unknown threats and address them before cybercriminals do. Target Audience This course is designed to prepare learners with the Ethical Hacker skillset. Learners will become proficient in the art of scoping, executing, and reporting on vulnerability assessments, while recommending mitigation strategies. By using an engaging gamified narrative throughout the course, with real-world inspired hands-on practice labs, learners develop essential workforce readiness skills to lay a solid foundation in offensive security. After completing this course, learners can enter cybersecurity careers, either on the offensive security side as ethical hackers or penetration testers, or on the defensive security side by understanding the mindset and tactics of threat actors, while implementing security controls and monitoring, analyzing, and responding to current security threats.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information - Students must complete all assignments on the Cisco Networking Academy (https://skillsforall.com/) with a result of at least 75%.
general_information.Tools: Internet, basic tools for ethical hacking (VMWare, Kali Linux, Wireshark, Nmap, …)
general_information.Note: 1) On-going Assessment + 02 Progress Test: 20% + Project: 30% + 12 Labs: 20% 2) 1 Final Exam: 30% 3) Completion criteria: Every on-going assessment component > 0, Final Result >=5, Average Lab Score >= 4 & Final Exam Score >=4

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Explain the importance of methodological ethical hacking and penetration testing.
Apply incident response models to manage network security incidents.
Perform information gathering and vulnerability scanning activities.
Explain how social engineering attacks succeed.
Explain how to exploit wired and wireless network vulnerabilities.
Explain how to exploit application-based vulnerabilities.
Explain how to exploit cloud, mobile, and IoT security vulnerabilities.
Explain how to perform post-exploitation activities; Create a penetration testing report; Classify pentesting tools by use case.
Evaluate network security alerts; Analyze network intrusion data to identify compromised hosts and vulnerabilities.

schedule.Topic: Module 1: Introduction to Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing 1.1 Understanding Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing Introduction to the Project
1.2 Exploring Penetration Testing Methodologies 1.3 Building Your Own Lab
LAB 1
LAB 1(cont)

Project : Group and topic register + Divide class into 3-5 groups + Group select the interesting topic Students form groups of 3–5 members in Session 5 to initiate the ethical hacking project. Groups establish roles (e.g., reconnaissance lead, exploit developer, report writer) and set collaboration protocols to ensure effective teamwork throughout the project.
Module 2: Planning and Scoping a Penetration Testing Assessment 2.1 Comparing and Contrasting Governance, Risk, and Compliance Concepts
Module 2:(cont) 2.2 Explaining the Importance of Scoping and Organizational or Customer Requirements 2.3 Demonstrating an Ethical Hacking Mindset by Maintaining Professionalism and Integrity
LAB 2: Lab_Pre-Engagement_Scope_and_Planning
Module 3: Information Gathering and Vulnerability Scanning 3.1 Performing Passive Reconnaissance 3.2 Performing Active Reconnaissance
Module 3: (cont) 3.3 Understanding the Art of Performing Vulnerability Scans 3.4 Understanding How to Analyze Vulnerability Scan Results
LAB 3
LAB 3: (cont)

Groups discuss and work on group topics Groups select a project topic in Session 5, choosing from: a simulated penetration test in a lab environment, a case study of a real-world ethical hacking incident, or development of a custom penetration testing tool. The problem definition outlines the target system, scenario, or case study context, specifying objectives like identifying vulnerabilities or analyzing attack impacts.
LAB 4: 4.1-Lab_Advanced_Searches 4.2-Lab-Packet_Crafting_with_Scapy 4.3-Lab_Network_Sniffing_with_Wireshark
LAB 5: 5.1-Lab-Vulnerability_Scanning_with-Kali_Tools 5.2-Lab-Investigate_Vulnerability_Information_Sources
LAB 5: (cont) 5.1-Lab-Vulnerability_Scanning_with-Kali_Tools 5.2-Lab-Investigate_Vulnerability_Information_Sources
Module 4: Social Engineering Attacks 4.1 Pretexting for an Approach and Impersonation 4.2 Social Engineering Attacks

Module 4: (cont) 4.3 Physical Attacks Conduct thorough research leveraging Modules 1–3 (e.g., ethical hacking concepts, penetration testing methodologies, reconnaissance techniques). Use resources like textbooks, OWASP guidelines, and NIST standards to understand the chosen topic’s technical and ethical scope.
Module 4: (cont) 4.4 Social Engineering Tools 4.5 Methods of Influence
LAB 6: 6.1-Lab_Explore_the_Social_Engineer_Toolkit_(SET)
LAB 6: (cont) 6.2-Lab_Using_the_Browser_Exploitation_Framework_(BeEF)
Module 5: Exploiting Wired and Wireless Networks 5.1 Exploiting Network-Based Vulnerabilities
Module 5: Exploiting Wired and Wireless Networks (Cont) 5.2 Exploiting Wireless Vulnerabilities Quiz1
LAB 7: 7.1-Lab_On-Path_Attacks_with_Ettercap 7.2-Lab_Scanning_for_SMB_Vulnerabilities_with_enum4linux

Groups discuss and work on group topics Perform reconnaissance (passive and active, per Module 3) to identify attack surfaces and vulnerabilities. Document potential threats (e.g., network-based, application-based, or social engineering attacks) and assess their risks using frameworks like NIST or CompTIA PenTest+.
Module 6: Exploiting Application-Based Vulnerabilities 6.1 Overview of Web Application-Based Attacks for Security Professionals and the OWASP Top 10 6.2 How to Build Your Own Web Application Lab
Module 6: Exploiting Application-Based Vulnerabilities (cont) 6.3 Understanding Business Logic Flaws 6.4 Understanding Injection-Based Vulnerabilities

Module 6: Exploiting Application-Based Vulnerabilities (cont) 6.5 Exploiting Authentication-Based Vulnerabilities 6.6 Exploiting Authorization-Based Vulnerabilities Design a penetration testing strategy or tool, aligned with Modules 3–6. For simulations, plan reconnaissance, scanning, and exploitation phases (e.g., using Kali Linux tools). For case studies, outline analytical approaches. For tool development, design scripts for tasks like vulnerability scanning or exploit automation.
Module 6: Exploiting Application-Based Vulnerabilities (cont) 6.7 Understanding Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerabilities
Module 6: Exploiting Application-Based Vulnerabilities (cont) 6.8 Understanding Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF/XSRF) and Server-Side Request Forgery Attacks
Module 6: Exploiting Application-Based Vulnerabilities (cont) 6.9 Understanding Clickjacking
Module 6: Exploiting Application-Based Vulnerabilities (cont) 6.10 Exploiting File Inclusion Vulnerabilities
Module 6: Exploiting Application-Based Vulnerabilities (cont) 6.11 Exploiting Insecure Code Practices
LAB 8: 8.1-Lab-Web_Vulnerability_Scanning 8.2-Lab-Using_the_GVM_Vulnerability_Scanner
LAB 9: 9.1-Lab-Injection_Attacks 9.2-Lab-Using_Password_Tools
LAB 9: (cont) 9.3-Lab-Cross_Site_Scripting

Groups discuss and work on group topics Use AI tools in to brainstorm attack vectors, generate code snippets (e.g., for reconnaissance or exploit scripts), or structure findings. Critically evaluate AI outputs for accuracy and relevance, documenting the validation process (e.g., cross-referencing with OWASP or testing in a lab environment).
Module 7: Cloud, Mobile, and IoT Security 7.1 Researching Attack Vectors and Performing Attacks on Cloud Technologies
Module 7: Cloud, Mobile, and IoT Security (cont) 7.2 Explaining Common Attacks and Vulnerabilities Against Specialized Systems
Module 8: Performing Post-Exploitation Techniques 8.1 Creating a Foothold and Maintaining Persistence After Compromising a System

Module 8: Performing Post-Exploitation Techniques (cont) 8.2 Understanding How to Perform Lateral Movement, Detection Avoidance, and Enumeration Execute the project: conduct penetration tests (e.g., exploiting XSS, SQL injection, or network vulnerabilities), analyze case studies with detailed attack breakdowns, or develop and test custom tools. Document all steps, including tools used (e.g., SET, BeEF, Wireshark) and outcomes.
Module 9: Reporting and Communication 9.1 Comparing and Contrasting Important Components of Written Reports 9.2 Analyzing the Findings and Recommending the Appropriate Remediation Within a Report
Module 9: Reporting and Communication (cont) 9.3 Explaining the Importance of Communication During the Penetration Testing Process 9.4 Explaining Post-Report Delivery Activities
Lab 10: 10.1-Lab-Explore_PenTest_Reports 10.2-Lab–Recommend_Remediation_Based_on_Findings

Groups discuss and work on group topics Draft an 8–12 page report covering the scenario overview, vulnerability assessment, exploitation/mitigation strategies, and AI usage reflection. Conduct peer reviews within the group to refine technical accuracy, clarity, and alignment with standards like OWASP or NIST, as per Module 9.
Module 10: Tools and Code Analysis 10.1 Understanding the Basic Concepts of Scripting and Software Development
Module 10: Tools and Code Analysis (cont) 10.2 Understanding the Different Use Cases of Penetration Testing Tools and Analyzing Exploit Code
LAB 11: 11.1-Lab–Analyze_Exploit_Code
LAB 11: (cont) 11.2-Lab–Analyze_Automation_Code
Module 11: Cryptography 11.1 Understanding Cryptography Basics 11.2 Understanding Symmetric and Asymmetric Algorithms
Module 11. Cryptography (cont.) 11.3 Components of PKI 11.4 Understanding Cryptography Attacks
LAB 12

Lab 12(cont) Report the progress of Project Finalize the report, incorporating peer feedback and ensuring compliance with ethical hacking standards. Prepare a 10–15 minute presentation with slides and, if applicable, live demos (e.g., tool execution or attack simulation), focusing on key findings and remediation strategies.
Module 12 Network. Protection Systems 12.1 Understanding Routers 12.2 Understanding Firewalls
Module 12 Network. Protection Systems (cont.) 12.3 Understanding Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems 12.3 Understanding Honeypots

Groups discuss and work on group topics Deliver the presentation, allocating 8–10 minutes for slides or demos and 5 minutes for Q&A. Peers will question technical details, ethical considerations, and mitigation approaches. Assessment criteria include communication clarity, technical depth, teamwork, and ability to defend findings, per Module 9.
Groups discuss and work on group topics
Group Present: Final report the Project
Group Present: Final report the Project (Cont)
